newsitem.title: POLAND: NATO to build flight-training centre in Poland.
newsitem.headline: NATO to build flight-training centre in Poland.

text.p: NATO has selected Poland as the site for a training centre for air force pilots from future member countries in Eastern Europe, public television reported late Saturday night.
The Polish centre, to be based at the Air Force Academy in Deblin, some 100 km (62 miles) southeast of Warsaw, will train pilots from Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary.
"One of the academy's main tasks will now be to train flight personnel with a view to our integration with NATO structures," Brigadier General Ryszard Olszewski told the television.

The report said the 70-year-old Polish academy, one of the world's oldest military-aviation schools, is internationally known for its modern training methods. It said NATO planned two flight training centres, the other in Canada.
Poland hopes its membership of NATO -- its top foreign-policy priority since the collapse of communism nearly eight years ago -- will become a reality within the next few years.
